approach.method_basis: The Parent draws local atom, bond, path and ring edits from one scored current molecule, including direct formula-preserving exchanges of aromatic nitrogen and carbon positions. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and evaluates the first full batch allowed by inverse-motif memory. A fresh neighbor is vetoed when its motif-count changes have both inverse signs associated with one recent selected transition. Memory retains at most four signed attributes per transition, ages over four completed steps and refreshes overlapping attributes to their latest origin. The walk moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a loss, while a separate archive retains the best observation. Its matching rule currently checks the sign of a count change but ignores how much of the earlier motif abundance is actually restored.
approach.novelty: Make inverse matching depend on the remembered occurrence-count boundary. A reverse change can support a veto only when its resulting motif count reaches or passes the count before the remembered transition; both inverse signs must still qualify from the same transition. This allows partial restoration of repeated environments while retaining exclusions that undo their remembered abundance change. Earlier siblings required every live attribute, changed which transitions or motifs received credit, or retained overlapping origins. This experiment changes the quantitative meaning of one attribute match, with the existing attribute selection and lifecycle preserved. Four recorded opportunities remain vetoed even by the earlier complete-signature rule, so the new boundary addresses a different mismatch.

hypothesis: Require each signed inverse-motif match to place the candidate destination occurrence count at or beyond that selected transition's pre-move count in the inverse direction before it can participate in the existing same-transition bidirectional tabu veto.

finding_summary.headline: Count boundaries admitted 11 evaluated neighbors, but reduced the panel mean by 0.0261
finding_summary.insights: Occurrence counts identify a real admission distinction that signed motif coverage alone misses: two of the eleven newly evaluated molecules still matched every live attribute of a qualifying transition. However, most count-ineligible matches were not allocation bottlenecks: 157 of 176 occurred in candidates already admitted by the parent's one-sign or cross-origin rules. The eleven actual admissions therefore establish changed allocation, not a general score advantage from more quantitatively specific memory. Source-beating proposals became slightly more frequent across the full stream, but their total positive gain and the total archive improvement both fell. Together with ten source-worsening new admissions and strongly different DRD2 outcomes across seeds, this narrows the useful question to which abundance reversals support productive exploration, rather than whether count boundaries are implemented correctly. The three selected admissions have real later descendants and archive gains, but those paths also include changed random-draw consumption and subsequent edits; their gains cannot be assigned to the admission alone. The stricter parent alternatives stopped short in all nine affected batches, so their missing members and scores remain unknown. The molecular assessment likewise finds no established improvement in practical chemistry: recognizable aromatic and amine families still coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur frameworks and undefined stereochemistry. Restoring motif abundance is neither a physical edit-site measurement nor evidence of chemical stability.

The deco_hop mean rose by 0.001763, zaleplon fell by 0.002347, and median_2 and sitagliptin retained exactly the same molecular trajectories and scores.

molecular.headline: Aromatic scaffolds and cyclic amines coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds, sulfur-rich cages, and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-ccfeef46a581 produces compact to relatively large, extensively branched ring-containing molecules. All supplied tasks have trajectories; the brief tasks_without_trajectories list is empty. Each task digest covers 900 evaluations, including 870 optimizer proposals. The optimizer-proposal ring_closure_rate and branch_rate are 1.0 on every task. In the fixed task order, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9517, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, and 0.7184; these are string-presence rates, not fractions of atoms or perceived aromatic rings. Mean SMILES lengths are 45.9, 69.6, 68.8, 61.0, and 62.8, respectively; text length is only a rough indication of molecular elaboration. Recognizable indole carboxamides, aryl ketones, cyclic amines, ureas, and lactams are present. They coexist with peroxide and nitrogen-halogen bonds, unconventional sulfur valences, nonbenzenoid small-ring unsaturation, and densely bridged polycycles. Charged_rate and stereocentre_rate are 0.0 throughout. This describes the submitted representations: many molecules contain potentially ionizable groups or stereogenic structures despite having no charge or tetrahedral stereochemical annotations. Across tasks and seeds there are distinct scaffold families, so diversity has not collapsed globally; within several best-molecule panels, closely related members of one seed-specific family dominate. Synthetic plausibility is mixed, with ordinary medicinal fragments embedded in structures whose stability, geometry, and practical assembly are doubtful. These are structural judgments, not synthesis predictions or activity measurements. All child and Parent trajectory records were read. Parent comparison shows exact molecular-history preservation for median_2 and sitagliptin_mpo, with changed families on the other tasks. The digest final_molecules excerpts contain the last proposals from seed 2; they are not all-seed final incumbents. The gradients below describe associations and occasional direct structural comparisons in the observed scores. They do not reveal hidden objective definitions or establish a specific missing target pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The relatively compact output is dominated by fused aromatic or partly aromatic heterocycles bearing aryl carboxamides or aryl ketones, with alkoxy, alkyl, amino, halogen, and sulfur substituents. The ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilide at 0.399050 is recognizable synthetic chemistry, though the free thiol adds reactivity. The maximum at 0.402997 instead combines an aminomethyl substituent, a thiocarboxylic acid, an S-bound nitrile, an unsaturated fused oxygen/sulfur ring system, and a bridged tertiary nitrogen group. The lowest optimizer excerpt at 0.021533 has an expanded, partly saturated ring and an N-fluoro hydroxylamine substituent. Late seed-2 proposals retain the unusual sulfur/bridged-amine framework. Relative to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc, the seed-0 and seed-1 best molecules and scores are identical; the seed-2 best changes from a substituted benzofuran aryl carboxamide at 0.410039 to the sulfur-containing bridged-amine structure at 0.402997. That structural change does not demonstrate improved makeability.
liabilities: Expanded-valence sulfur, a thiocarboxylic acid, and the bridged unsaturated nitrogen group make the maximum less straightforward to synthesize than its near-scoring indole carboxamide comparator.
N-fluoro hydroxylamine, nitrogen-bromine, and cyclic cumulated-double-bond motifs occur in the trajectory excerpts. The digest cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.1149.
The new bridged structures have no stereochemical assignments, so the scored strings do not define a single stereochemical product.
missing_features: Compact aromatic-carbonyl organization and the productive aminomethyl spacing are not consistently retained in the low-score and late edited molecules, even though higher-scoring examples show them.

A well-defined, ordinary-valence series preserving the newly favored nitrogen placement while avoiding the bridged sulfur framework is not established by these excerpts; its score benefit remains unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxamide scores 0.305105, while the ethoxy/methyl/thiol analogue scores 0.399050. A carbonyl-disrupted aminoalkyl analogue in the low excerpt scores 0.033430, and the expanded partly saturated structure scores 0.021533; the observed contrast is consistent with preserving a compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement. There is also a more specific comparison: replacing the maximum molecule's aminomethyl group with fluoromethyl gives 0.329946, and shortening it to a directly attached amino group gives 0.330107. The placement and spacing of this nitrogen therefore matter in this observed scaffold. Neither conventional valence nor an entirely aromatic framework is sufficient to explain the ranking: the expanded-valence sulfur maximum slightly exceeds the ordinary indole carboxamide, and cyclic cumulated-double-bond analogues appear at 0.386646.

per_task.generated_character: These are comparatively large, heavily substituted aromatic molecules; mean SMILES length is 69.6, and every proposal has both ring-closure and aromatic-atom text. The 0.617463 maximum contains a phenyl-pyridyl diarylamine assembly, a furan carrying a substituted urea, an aryl imine, a methylthio group, an O-O-N substituent bearing bromine on nitrogen, and a terminal thiocarbonyl chain. The seed-2 final excerpt instead contains fused nitrogen heterocyclic diones, a fused aza ring system, a flexible polyene side chain, and alkoxy-rich branches. The low 0.518907 excerpt is a crowded bridged heterocycle retaining an ester and amide-type carbonyls but disrupting much of the ordinary aromatic organization. Compared with the Parent, the seed-0 maximum changes from 0.616171 to 0.617463 and the seed-1 maximum from 0.605140 to 0.609136, while the seed-2 trajectory is molecularly identical. The changed branches continue to produce extensively decorated aromatic and nitrogen/sulfur-rich structures; they do not establish a consistently simple synthetic series.
liabilities: The best series combines peroxide, nitrogen-halogen, and terminal thiocarbonyl functionality, raising stability and practical synthesis concerns despite high scores.

The large polyene/alkoxy branches and heavily bridged alternatives create conformational and assembly complexity; double-bond and tetrahedral configurations are not explicitly defined in the cited examples.
Halogen_rate is 0.7425, but some halogens are bonded to nitrogen rather than residing only in conventional carbon-halogen substituents.
missing_features: Stable, ordinary-linkage realizations of the highly decorated aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are not represented as a coherent high-scoring comparison series; the leading family repeatedly carries peroxide-linked nitrogen and thiocarbonyl appendages.

Controlled comparisons that preserve the useful aromatic attachment pattern while simplifying flexible branches and bridges are missing. The score ties do not justify inventing a specific hidden decoration or binding geometry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381. Higher values accompany elaborated aromatic/aza-aromatic connectivity retaining urea or dione carbonyls, while the disrupted bridged low excerpt scores 0.518907. This is a multifeature association, not proof that adding bulk or a particular functional group causes improvement. The digest contains an exact 0.617402 tie between an open diarylamine derivative, a bridged derivative, and a derivative with chlorine replacing a methyl group on the peroxide-linked nitrogen. Those equal scores show that the observed high region does not reliably distinguish these changes in geometry or chemical liability. The separate dione/polyene family also reaches 0.609218, so a unique required terminal decoration cannot be identified from these trajectories.

per_task.generated_character: The output spans bulky acid/amide/sulfonamide polyaryls, more compact polycyclic amines, and sulfur-rich bridged structures. The 0.999999 maximum is an N-methyl tetrahydroisoquinoline-like scaffold bearing an amino-substituted azetidine through a methylene linker, together with an ethyl group, aryl fluorine, methoxy, and a thioether-linked nonbenzenoid fused small-ring group. It contains recognizable potentially basic cyclic amines and an exocyclic primary amine, all encoded neutrally. The 0.006990 low excerpt retains carboxylic acid, amide, and N-sulfonylated cyclic nitrogen functionality in a larger polyaryl molecule. The final seed-2 excerpt instead has dense sulfur-containing bridges, multiple nitrogen/oxygen linkages, and sulfur-carbon triple bonding; it is chemically very different from the seed-0 maximum. Parent comparison is heterogeneous: the seed-0 maximum changes from 0.885624 to 0.999999 with a less sulfur-heavy amine scaffold, while the other seed maxima change from 0.868020 to 0.806462 and from 0.914814 to 0.471973. The single near-unity maximum therefore does not characterize every trajectory.
liabilities: The high series combines ordinary saturated nitrogen rings with an unusual fused unsaturated small-ring group; recognizing the amine scaffold does not validate the appended ring geometry.
A high-scoring hydroperoxide analogue and late expanded-valence sulfur, sulfur-carbon triple bonds, and nitrogen-oxygen/nitrogen-nitrogen linkages raise distinct stability concerns.
Halogen_rate is 0.9977. The molecules also have unassigned stereogenic structures despite the universal absence of stereocentre annotations.
missing_features: The compact cyclic-amine/aryl organization seen in the high seed-0 series is not reproduced cleanly in the other trajectories, which retain heavily bridged and sulfur-rich structures.
Chemically interpretable alternatives to the nonbenzenoid small-ring appendage, with the same amine presentation and defined stereochemistry, are not established as a scored series.
Explicit protonation alternatives are absent despite potentially ionizable amines. The trajectories provide no direct charge-state comparison, so a charge-related score benefit cannot be asserted.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The high seed-0 series replaces much of the low series's acid, amide, and sulfonamide burden with compact cyclic amines and differently positioned hydrophobic ring groups. That supports an association with amine presentation and molecular organization, not a conclusion about a particular receptor interaction. Amine presence alone is insufficient: the initial N-methylpiperidine-containing molecule scores 0.000379. A hydroperoxide-containing analogue remains at 0.999994, close to the 0.999999 maximum, showing that this high-score region tolerates a conspicuous chemical liability. The final seed-2 sulfur-rich example scores 0.210570, while a related example replacing one sulfur centre with carbon scores 0.343373. This local contrast supports sensitivity to the represented sulfur framework, without explaining the whole between-seed difference.

per_task.generated_character: The molecules are medium to large aromatic heterocycles with substantial ring bridging and amide-derived functionality; mean SMILES length is 61.0 and aromatic_atom_rate is 1.0. The 0.211969 maximum contains pyridyl and tolyl groups, alkyl substituents, an alkene, an N-methyl lactam, and an N-O bridge in a densely connected polycyclic framework. The high excerpt mainly varies the alkyl groups and bridge composition around this family. The low 0.124680 example is a more open aryl/pyrrole ester-phenol scaffold with a flexible ketone/urea/hydrazine-bearing branch. Another low example carries organic hypobromite and brominated side-chain functionality. The final seed-2 excerpt has a bridged sulfur/nitrogen dicarbonyl system with aromatic and hydroxymethyl/alkoxy substituents. Every molecular record and score in the child trajectories matches the Parent for this task, including the 0.211969 best structure. Ordinary lactam and aromatic fragments are present, but the recurring bridge networks and N-O chemistry make the whole structures synthetically questionable.
liabilities: The leading series contains N-O bridges, and a nearly scoring analogue contains an O-O bond within that bridge; these linkages complicate stability and synthetic interpretation.
Dense overlapping ring closures and unspecified stereogenic centres make a single practical three-dimensional product difficult to infer from the strings.
Other branches add organic hypobromites and unconventional sulfur bonding; the observed ring richness is not evidence that those assemblies are readily makeable.
missing_features: A broader set of chemically ordinary arrangements that retain the leading aromatic/lactam relationships without the crowded N-O bridge network is not established by the high-molecule panel.
The constrained structures lack stereochemical definition. Whether resolving those configurations would change this score is not observable here.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused-dione molecule scores 0.167839, the open ketone/urea/hydrazine example 0.124680, and the constrained lactam/N-O-bridged maximum 0.211969. Within the leading family, extending the carbon substituent at the ring bridge from methyl to ethyl changes 0.208747 to 0.211969. The observed gradient therefore contains both a preference for this particular constrained aromatic/lactam organization over the shown open analogues and only modest local sensitivity to alkyl elaboration. An additional oxygen in the N-O bridge gives a peroxide-containing analogue at 0.206478, so nearly retaining the score does not establish chemical stability. These structures and scores do not identify an absent reference scaffold or prove that more bridges generally improve the objective.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are densely cyclized, sulfur-rich, fluorinated heterocycles rather than a simple amine/amide series. Mean SMILES length is 62.8; ring_closure_rate is 1.0, while aromatic_atom_rate is 0.7184, consistent with the substantial nonaromatic cage chemistry in the trajectories. The 0.590353 maximum combines a nitrogen heterocyclic dione, carbon-fluorine substituents, an alcohol-bearing fluoro carbon attached to sulfur, sulfur-sulfur connectivity, and expanded-valence sulfur embedded in multiple fused and bridged rings. A high seed-0 example at 0.481186 has a still more sulfur-heavy framework, an acyl fluoride, and sulfur-nitrogen functionality. The seed-2 final family contains a cyclic thioester/carbonyl framework, aldehyde or sulfur-containing acyl branches, an imidoyl nitrogen group with N-F connectivity, and dense bridges; it includes the 0.448455 seed-2 best. All child molecular records and scores for this task reproduce the Parent exactly. The sulfur valences, reactive appendages, and unspecified stereochemical relationships make these among the least synthetically convincing structures in the panel.
liabilities: Repeated expanded-valence sulfur and sulfur-sulfur bonds are incorporated directly into constrained unsaturated cages; graph readability does not establish stable bonding or feasible geometry.
The cited examples contain an acyl fluoride, N-F bonds, an aldehyde, and a sulfur-chlorine acyl substituent. These are reactive functionality concerns, not measured toxicity claims.
Extensive fused and bridged ring construction leaves stereogenic relationships unspecified; the neutral strings do not define single stereochemical synthetic products.
missing_features: The trajectories do not establish ordinary-valence, synthetically interpretable analogues that preserve the favorable local fluorinated carbonyl/nitrogen arrangement; the observed higher scores remain tied to highly unusual cage chemistry.
The densely fused structures have no assigned stereochemistry or demonstrated spatial feasibility. No score comparison establishes an advantage for a particular configuration.

A clean matched series separating fluorine placement, carbonyl spacing, and sulfur substitution is absent from the leading examples, so a specific missing functional group cannot be justified from this evidence alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic ester/phenol fused dione scores 0.002094, and an expanded-ring derivative retaining that general decoration scores only 7.590554525032884e-10. Higher scores occur after major reorganization into compact fluorinated sulfur-containing frameworks while carbonyl/nitrogen functionality remains in altered arrangements. Fluorination or sulfur enrichment alone cannot explain the gradient: the low digest also contains already sulfur-rich, fluorinated polycycles. Within the late seed-2 family, related carbonyl/linker variants score 0.253662 and 0.448455, while the sulfur-containing acyl-branch variant scores 0.004200. This shows strong sensitivity to the particular composition and connectivity around the cage and carbonyl groups. It does not demonstrate that unusual sulfur chemistry is itself desirable or that a known target pharmacophore is missing.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the supplied best, low, and late excerpts, recognizable amides, ureas, lactams, and amines coexist with O-O bonds, nitrogen-halogen bonds, terminal thiocarbonyls, and expanded-valence sulfur. A peroxide-bearing cyclic-amine analogue scores 0.999994, and an O-O-N-linked aromatic urea series reaches 0.617463, demonstrating that these liabilities can survive into high-scoring output. The limitation is therefore not a complete absence of useful functional groups; their chemically ordinary context is not maintained.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve chemically ordinary, stable functional-group connectivity during elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs accessible edits that preserve complete functional-group contexts and produce ordinary-valence analogues of the existing favorable arrangements. Bond proposals and heteroatom substitutions can use the local molecular environment to distinguish conventional amide, ether, amine, and thioether chemistry from reactive or unusual combinations. Any effect on the observed objective scores requires a separate evaluation; these structural concerns do not justify assuming a universal score gain from filtering.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every optimizer proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0. The cited high and final structures include densely overlapping bridges, nonbenzenoid fused small-ring unsaturation, cyclic cumulated double bonds, and sulfur-centred multiple bonding. Ordinary indole, saturated cyclic-amine, and lactam fragments are also present, so the missing capability is controlled ring architecture rather than ring creation itself.
transferable_gaps.gap: Abundant ring construction is not accompanied by consistent control over chemically credible ring geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need to propose and retain more interpretable ring and linker arrangements at comparable functionality, using molecule-local topology and geometry plausibility to distinguish ordinary saturated/fused systems from strained unsaturated closures. Conventional small saturated rings should remain accessible; the evidence supports examining the particular bonding and bridge context, not banning every small ring or assuming a particular ring family must score better.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 in every proposal set. The cited substituted cyclic amines and sulfur-rich bridged frameworks contain stereogenic arrangements whose configurations are left unspecified. The gap concerns representation of the produced molecules; the supplied scores provide no comparison between assigned configurations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated structures do not include explicit tetrahedral stereochemical definition despite recurring stereogenic polycycles.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to recognize stereogenic elements and make chemically valid configuration assignment or variation available while preserving explicit isomeric identity. Configuration choices should follow the actual molecular graph and observed feedback, without assuming a preferred configuration or inventing task-specific stereochemical requirements.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Charged_rate is 0.0 on every task despite cited primary and tertiary cyclic amines, carboxylic acids, and thiocarboxylic acids. High-scoring amine-bearing structures are therefore represented only in neutral form in these trajectories; the digest contains no evidence that a different charge state would improve a score.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ionizable functional groups are produced without an observed set of explicit charge or protonation alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need molecule-local support for chemically valid protonation and formal-charge alternatives, with the chosen representation kept explicit and consistent. This would address missing chemical-state coverage; its usefulness must be tested through allowed feedback rather than inferred from an objective name or from unmeasured pKa values.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The full panel contains distinct aromatic amide, cyclic-amine, lactam, and sulfur-cage families, supporting moderate overall diversity. Several best-molecule excerpts nevertheless repeat a single seed-specific scaffold through alkyl, halogen, or bridge changes, and the final excerpts can retain the same unusual heteroatom framework. The numerous unique strings do not by themselves establish broad coverage of ordinary alternative scaffolds around the useful functional groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring output has limited scaffold variety at a preserved, interpretable functional-group arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need scaffold and linker rearrangements that preserve recognizable functional groups and their relative attachment pattern while offering different, chemically ordinary ring architectures. Such proposals should be driven by the currently observed molecules and scores; the trajectories do not supply a universal desired scaffold or justify choosing a benchmark-specific motif.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

applicability_conditions: The mechanism matters when recurring motifs change by multiple occurrences or subsequent selected moves shift their counts before an inverse candidate appears. The threshold is the selected transition's absolute pre-move occurrence count. For an inverse increase the candidate endpoint must be at least that count; for an inverse decrease it must be at most that count. The candidate must independently have the matching nonzero signed change. Its starting count need not be on the opposite side, so this is an endpoint-side condition rather than a required crossing event or one-step magnitude test.

Counts are whole-molecule multiplicities of the inherited interpretable rooted radius-one motifs. A fresh neighbor is vetoed when its motif-count changes have both inverse signs associated with one recent selected transition. Memory retains at most four signed attributes per transition, ages over four completed steps and refreshes overlapping attributes to their latest origin. The walk moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a loss, while a separate archive retains the best observation. Its matching rule currently checks the sign of a count change but ignores how much of the earlier motif abundance is actually restored.
approach.novelty: Make inverse matching depend on the remembered occurrence-count boundary. A reverse change can support a veto only when its resulting motif count reaches or passes the count before the remembered transition; both inverse signs must still qualify from the same transition. This allows partial restoration of repeated environments while retaining exclusions that undo their remembered abundance change. Earlier siblings required every live attribute, changed which transitions or motifs received credit, or retained overlapping origins. This experiment changes the quantitative meaning of one attribute match, with the existing attribute selection and lifecycle preserved. Four recorded opportunities remain vetoed even by the earlier complete-signature rule, so the new boundary addresses a different mismatch.

finding_summary.headline: Count boundaries admitted 11 evaluated neighbors, but reduced the panel mean by 0.0261
finding_summary.insights: Occurrence counts identify a real admission distinction that signed motif coverage alone misses: two of the eleven newly evaluated molecules still matched every live attribute of a qualifying transition. Source-beating proposals became slightly more frequent across the full stream, but their total positive gain and the total archive improvement both fell. The stricter parent alternatives stopped short in all nine affected batches, so their missing members and scores remain unknown. molecular_assessment.headline: Aromatic scaffolds and cyclic amines coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds, sulfur-rich cages, and undefined stereochemistry
molecular_assessment.overall_character: Node n-ccfeef46a581 produces compact to relatively large, extensively branched ring-containing molecules. All supplied tasks have trajectories; the brief tasks_without_trajectories list is empty. Each task digest covers 900 evaluations, including 870 optimizer proposals. The optimizer-proposal ring_closure_rate and branch_rate are 1.0 on every task. In the fixed task order, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9517, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, and 0.7184; these are string-presence rates, not fractions of atoms or perceived aromatic rings. Mean SMILES lengths are 45.9, 69.6, 68.8, 61.0, and 62.8, respectively; text length is only a rough indication of molecular elaboration. Recognizable indole carboxamides, aryl ketones, cyclic amines, ureas, and lactams are present. They coexist with peroxide and nitrogen-halogen bonds, unconventional sulfur valences, nonbenzenoid small-ring unsaturation, and densely bridged polycycles. Charged_rate and stereocentre_rate are 0.0 throughout. This describes the submitted representations: many molecules contain potentially ionizable groups or stereogenic structures despite having no charge or tetrahedral stereochemical annotations. Across tasks and seeds there are distinct scaffold families, so diversity has not collapsed globally; within several best-molecule panels, closely related members of one seed-specific family dominate. Synthetic plausibility is mixed, with ordinary medicinal fragments embedded in structures whose stability, geometry, and practical assembly are doubtful. These are structural judgments, not synthesis predictions or activity measurements. All child and Parent trajectory records were read. Parent comparison shows exact molecular-history preservation for median_2 and sitagliptin_mpo, with changed families on the other tasks. The digest final_molecules excerpts contain the last proposals from seed 2; they are not all-seed final incumbents. The gradients below describe associations and occasional direct structural comparisons in the observed scores. They do not reveal hidden objective definitions or establish a specific missing target pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The relatively compact output is dominated by fused aromatic or partly aromatic heterocycles bearing aryl carboxamides or aryl ketones, with alkoxy, alkyl, amino, halogen, and sulfur substituents. The ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilide at 0.399050 is recognizable synthetic chemistry, though the free thiol adds reactivity. The maximum at 0.402997 instead combines an aminomethyl substituent, a thiocarboxylic acid, an S-bound nitrile, an unsaturated fused oxygen/sulfur ring system, and a bridged tertiary nitrogen group. The lowest optimizer excerpt at 0.021533 has an expanded, partly saturated ring and an N-fluoro hydroxylamine substituent. Late seed-2 proposals retain the unusual sulfur/bridged-amine framework. Relative to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc, the seed-0 and seed-1 best molecules and scores are identical; the seed-2 best changes from a substituted benzofuran aryl carboxamide at 0.410039 to the sulfur-containing bridged-amine structure at 0.402997. That structural change does not demonstrate improved makeability.
liabilities: Expanded-valence sulfur, a thiocarboxylic acid, and the bridged unsaturated nitrogen group make the maximum less straightforward to synthesize than its near-scoring indole carboxamide comparator.
N-fluoro hydroxylamine, nitrogen-bromine, and cyclic cumulated-double-bond motifs occur in the trajectory excerpts. The digest cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.1149.
The new bridged structures have no stereochemical assignments, so the scored strings do not define a single stereochemical product.
missing_features: Compact aromatic-carbonyl organization and the productive aminomethyl spacing are not consistently retained in the low-score and late edited molecules, even though higher-scoring examples show them.

A well-defined, ordinary-valence series preserving the newly favored nitrogen placement while avoiding the bridged sulfur framework is not established by these excerpts; its score benefit remains unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxamide scores 0.305105, while the ethoxy/methyl/thiol analogue scores 0.399050. A carbonyl-disrupted aminoalkyl analogue in the low excerpt scores 0.033430, and the expanded partly saturated structure scores 0.021533; the observed contrast is consistent with preserving a compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement. There is also a more specific comparison: replacing the maximum molecule's aminomethyl group with fluoromethyl gives 0.329946, and shortening it to a directly attached amino group gives 0.330107. The placement and spacing of this nitrogen therefore matter in this observed scaffold. Neither conventional valence nor an entirely aromatic framework is sufficient to explain the ranking: the expanded-valence sulfur maximum slightly exceeds the ordinary indole carboxamide, and cyclic cumulated-double-bond analogues appear at 0.386646.

The large polyene/alkoxy branches and heavily bridged alternatives create conformational and assembly complexity; double-bond and tetrahedral configurations are not explicitly defined in the cited examples.
Halogen_rate is 0.7425, but some halogens are bonded to nitrogen rather than residing only in conventional carbon-halogen substituents.

Controlled comparisons that preserve the useful aromatic attachment pattern while simplifying flexible branches and bridges are missing. The score ties do not justify inventing a specific hidden decoration or binding geometry.

Higher values accompany elaborated aromatic/aza-aromatic connectivity retaining urea or dione carbonyls, while the disrupted bridged low excerpt scores 0.518907. This is a multifeature association, not proof that adding bulk or a particular functional group causes improvement. The digest contains an exact 0.617402 tie between an open diarylamine derivative, a bridged derivative, and a derivative with chlorine replacing a methyl group on the peroxide-linked nitrogen. Those equal scores show that the observed high region does not reliably distinguish these changes in geometry or chemical liability. The separate dione/polyene family also reaches 0.609218, so a unique required terminal decoration cannot be identified from these trajectories.

per_task.generated_character: The output spans bulky acid/amide/sulfonamide polyaryls, more compact polycyclic amines, and sulfur-rich bridged structures. The 0.999999 maximum is an N-methyl tetrahydroisoquinoline-like scaffold bearing an amino-substituted azetidine through a methylene linker, together with an ethyl group, aryl fluorine, methoxy, and a thioether-linked nonbenzenoid fused small-ring group. It contains recognizable potentially basic cyclic amines and an exocyclic primary amine, all encoded neutrally. The 0.006990 low excerpt retains carboxylic acid, amide, and N-sulfonylated cyclic nitrogen functionality in a larger polyaryl molecule. The final seed-2 excerpt instead has dense sulfur-containing bridges, multiple nitrogen/oxygen linkages, and sulfur-carbon triple bonding; it is chemically very different from the seed-0 maximum. Parent comparison is heterogeneous: the seed-0 maximum changes from 0.885624 to 0.999999 with a less sulfur-heavy amine scaffold, while the other seed maxima change from 0.868020 to 0.806462 and from 0.914814 to 0.471973. The single near-unity maximum therefore does not characterize every trajectory.
liabilities: The high series combines ordinary saturated nitrogen rings with an unusual fused unsaturated small-ring group; recognizing the amine scaffold does not validate the appended ring geometry.
A high-scoring hydroperoxide analogue and late expanded-valence sulfur, sulfur-carbon triple bonds, and nitrogen-oxygen/nitrogen-nitrogen linkages raise distinct stability concerns.
Halogen_rate is 0.9977. The molecules also have unassigned stereogenic structures despite the universal absence of stereocentre annotations.
missing_features: The compact cyclic-amine/aryl organization seen in the high seed-0 series is not reproduced cleanly in the other trajectories, which retain heavily bridged and sulfur-rich structures.
Chemically interpretable alternatives to the nonbenzenoid small-ring appendage, with the same amine presentation and defined stereochemistry, are not established as a scored series.
Explicit protonation alternatives are absent despite potentially ionizable amines. The trajectories provide no direct charge-state comparison, so a charge-related score benefit cannot be asserted.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The high seed-0 series replaces much of the low series's acid, amide, and sulfonamide burden with compact cyclic amines and differently positioned hydrophobic ring groups. That supports an association with amine presentation and molecular organization, not a conclusion about a particular receptor interaction. Amine presence alone is insufficient: the initial N-methylpiperidine-containing molecule scores 0.000379. A hydroperoxide-containing analogue remains at 0.999994, close to the 0.999999 maximum, showing that this high-score region tolerates a conspicuous chemical liability. The final seed-2 sulfur-rich example scores 0.210570, while a related example replacing one sulfur centre with carbon scores 0.343373. This local contrast supports sensitivity to the represented sulfur framework, without explaining the whole between-seed difference.

per_task.generated_character: The molecules are medium to large aromatic heterocycles with substantial ring bridging and amide-derived functionality; mean SMILES length is 61.0 and aromatic_atom_rate is 1.0. The 0.211969 maximum contains pyridyl and tolyl groups, alkyl substituents, an alkene, an N-methyl lactam, and an N-O bridge in a densely connected polycyclic framework. The high excerpt mainly varies the alkyl groups and bridge composition around this family. The low 0.124680 example is a more open aryl/pyrrole ester-phenol scaffold with a flexible ketone/urea/hydrazine-bearing branch. Another low example carries organic hypobromite and brominated side-chain functionality. The final seed-2 excerpt has a bridged sulfur/nitrogen dicarbonyl system with aromatic and hydroxymethyl/alkoxy substituents. Every molecular record and score in the child trajectories matches the Parent for this task, including the 0.211969 best structure. Ordinary lactam and aromatic fragments are present, but the recurring bridge networks and N-O chemistry make the whole structures synthetically questionable.
liabilities: The leading series contains N-O bridges, and a nearly scoring analogue contains an O-O bond within that bridge; these linkages complicate stability and synthetic interpretation.
Dense overlapping ring closures and unspecified stereogenic centres make a single practical three-dimensional product difficult to infer from the strings.
Other branches add organic hypobromites and unconventional sulfur bonding; the observed ring richness is not evidence that those assemblies are readily makeable.
missing_features: A broader set of chemically ordinary arrangements that retain the leading aromatic/lactam relationships without the crowded N-O bridge network is not established by the high-molecule panel.
The constrained structures lack stereochemical definition. Whether resolving those configurations would change this score is not observable here.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused-dione molecule scores 0.167839, the open ketone/urea/hydrazine example 0.124680, and the constrained lactam/N-O-bridged maximum 0.211969. Within the leading family, extending the carbon substituent at the ring bridge from methyl to ethyl changes 0.208747 to 0.211969. The observed gradient therefore contains both a preference for this particular constrained aromatic/lactam organization over the shown open analogues and only modest local sensitivity to alkyl elaboration. An additional oxygen in the N-O bridge gives a peroxide-containing analogue at 0.206478, so nearly retaining the score does not establish chemical stability. These structures and scores do not identify an absent reference scaffold or prove that more bridges generally improve the objective.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are densely cyclized, sulfur-rich, fluorinated heterocycles rather than a simple amine/amide series. Mean SMILES length is 62.8; ring_closure_rate is 1.0, while aromatic_atom_rate is 0.7184, consistent with the substantial nonaromatic cage chemistry in the trajectories. The 0.590353 maximum combines a nitrogen heterocyclic dione, carbon-fluorine substituents, an alcohol-bearing fluoro carbon attached to sulfur, sulfur-sulfur connectivity, and expanded-valence sulfur embedded in multiple fused and bridged rings. A high seed-0 example at 0.481186 has a still more sulfur-heavy framework, an acyl fluoride, and sulfur-nitrogen functionality. The seed-2 final family contains a cyclic thioester/carbonyl framework, aldehyde or sulfur-containing acyl branches, an imidoyl nitrogen group with N-F connectivity, and dense bridges; it includes the 0.448455 seed-2 best. All child molecular records and scores for this task reproduce the Parent exactly. The sulfur valences, reactive appendages, and unspecified stereochemical relationships make these among the least synthetically convincing structures in the panel.
liabilities: Repeated expanded-valence sulfur and sulfur-sulfur bonds are incorporated directly into constrained unsaturated cages; graph readability does not establish stable bonding or feasible geometry.
The cited examples contain an acyl fluoride, N-F bonds, an aldehyde, and a sulfur-chlorine acyl substituent. These are reactive functionality concerns, not measured toxicity claims.
Extensive fused and bridged ring construction leaves stereogenic relationships unspecified; the neutral strings do not define single stereochemical synthetic products.
missing_features: The trajectories do not establish ordinary-valence, synthetically interpretable analogues that preserve the favorable local fluorinated carbonyl/nitrogen arrangement; the observed higher scores remain tied to highly unusual cage chemistry.
The densely fused structures have no assigned stereochemistry or demonstrated spatial feasibility. No score comparison establishes an advantage for a particular configuration.

A clean matched series separating fluorine placement, carbonyl spacing, and sulfur substitution is absent from the leading examples, so a specific missing functional group cannot be justified from this evidence alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic ester/phenol fused dione scores 0.002094, and an expanded-ring derivative retaining that general decoration scores only 7.590554525032884e-10. Higher scores occur after major reorganization into compact fluorinated sulfur-containing frameworks while carbonyl/nitrogen functionality remains in altered arrangements. Fluorination or sulfur enrichment alone cannot explain the gradient: the low digest also contains already sulfur-rich, fluorinated polycycles. Within the late seed-2 family, related carbonyl/linker variants score 0.253662 and 0.448455, while the sulfur-containing acyl-branch variant scores 0.004200. This shows strong sensitivity to the particular composition and connectivity around the cage and carbonyl groups. It does not demonstrate that unusual sulfur chemistry is itself desirable or that a known target pharmacophore is missing.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the supplied best, low, and late excerpts, recognizable amides, ureas, lactams, and amines coexist with O-O bonds, nitrogen-halogen bonds, terminal thiocarbonyls, and expanded-valence sulfur. A peroxide-bearing cyclic-amine analogue scores 0.999994, and an O-O-N-linked aromatic urea series reaches 0.617463, demonstrating that these liabilities can survive into high-scoring output. The limitation is therefore not a complete absence of useful functional groups; their chemically ordinary context is not maintained.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve chemically ordinary, stable functional-group connectivity during elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs accessible edits that preserve complete functional-group contexts and produce ordinary-valence analogues of the existing favorable arrangements. Bond proposals and heteroatom substitutions can use the local molecular environment to distinguish conventional amide, ether, amine, and thioether chemistry from reactive or unusual combinations. Any effect on the observed objective scores requires a separate evaluation; these structural concerns do not justify assuming a universal score gain from filtering.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every optimizer proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0. The cited high and final structures include densely overlapping bridges, nonbenzenoid fused small-ring unsaturation, cyclic cumulated double bonds, and sulfur-centred multiple bonding. Ordinary indole, saturated cyclic-amine, and lactam fragments are also present, so the missing capability is controlled ring architecture rather than ring creation itself.
transferable_gaps.gap: Abundant ring construction is not accompanied by consistent control over chemically credible ring geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need to propose and retain more interpretable ring and linker arrangements at comparable functionality, using molecule-local topology and geometry plausibility to distinguish ordinary saturated/fused systems from strained unsaturated closures. Conventional small saturated rings should remain accessible; the evidence supports examining the particular bonding and bridge context, not banning every small ring or assuming a particular ring family must score better.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 in every proposal set. The cited substituted cyclic amines and sulfur-rich bridged frameworks contain stereogenic arrangements whose configurations are left unspecified. The gap concerns representation of the produced molecules; the supplied scores provide no comparison between assigned configurations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated structures do not include explicit tetrahedral stereochemical definition despite recurring stereogenic polycycles.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to recognize stereogenic elements and make chemically valid configuration assignment or variation available while preserving explicit isomeric identity. Configuration choices should follow the actual molecular graph and observed feedback, without assuming a preferred configuration or inventing task-specific stereochemical requirements.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Charged_rate is 0.0 on every task despite cited primary and tertiary cyclic amines, carboxylic acids, and thiocarboxylic acids. High-scoring amine-bearing structures are therefore represented only in neutral form in these trajectories; the digest contains no evidence that a different charge state would improve a score.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ionizable functional groups are produced without an observed set of explicit charge or protonation alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need molecule-local support for chemically valid protonation and formal-charge alternatives, with the chosen representation kept explicit and consistent. This would address missing chemical-state coverage; its usefulness must be tested through allowed feedback rather than inferred from an objective name or from unmeasured pKa values.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The full panel contains distinct aromatic amide, cyclic-amine, lactam, and sulfur-cage families, supporting moderate overall diversity. Several best-molecule excerpts nevertheless repeat a single seed-specific scaffold through alkyl, halogen, or bridge changes, and the final excerpts can retain the same unusual heteroatom framework. The numerous unique strings do not by themselves establish broad coverage of ordinary alternative scaffolds around the useful functional groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring output has limited scaffold variety at a preserved, interpretable functional-group arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need scaffold and linker rearrangements that preserve recognizable functional groups and their relative attachment pattern while offering different, chemically ordinary ring architectures. Such proposals should be driven by the currently observed molecules and scores; the trajectories do not supply a universal desired scaffold or justify choosing a benchmark-specific motif.

applicability_conditions: The mechanism matters when recurring motifs change by multiple occurrences or subsequent selected moves shift their counts before an inverse candidate appears. A changed source graph can have different exposure than the Parent's seven observed sessions; the experiment adds no quota or tuned threshold to force it.

The threshold is the selected transition's absolute pre-move occurrence count. For an inverse increase the candidate endpoint must be at least that count; for an inverse decrease it must be at most that count. The candidate must independently have the matching nonzero signed change. Its starting count need not be on the opposite side, so this is an endpoint-side condition rather than a required crossing event or one-step magnitude test.

Counts are whole-molecule multiplicities of the inherited interpretable rooted radius-one motifs. Returning their abundance does not identify the original atom positions, restore an entire molecule or establish chemical stability. Partial abundance changes can still remove important functionality, and strict count matching may weaken useful diversification.

The rule is an admissibility superset only at identical current graphs, candidates, completed steps and live tables. Earlier changed emissions alter seen sets, stochastic draw consumption and later accepted states, so total veto counts or final scores need not follow that ordering.

Only actual selected accepted transitions supply count boundaries. Unconditional winner selection, losing moves, archive independence, latest-overlap refresh and memory aging remain inherited; no hidden objective identity, unobserved label or score aspiration is used.

The current Parent includes aromatic nitrogen relocation and the identity repair, but none of the four earlier memory interventions. This experiment does not combine their credit, complete-signature, overlap or turnover changes. The supplied stage and batch resources remain fixed.

approach.method_basis: The Parent draws local atom, bond, path and ring edits from one scored current molecule, including direct formula-preserving exchanges of aromatic nitrogen and carbon positions. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and evaluates the first full batch allowed by inverse-motif memory. A fresh neighbor is vetoed when its motif-count changes have both inverse signs associated with one recent selected transition. Memory retains at most four signed attributes per transition, ages over four completed steps and refreshes overlapping attributes to their latest origin. The walk moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a loss, while a separate archive retains the best observation. Its matching rule currently checks the sign of a count change but ignores how much of the earlier motif abundance is actually restored.
approach.novelty: Make inverse matching depend on the remembered occurrence-count boundary. A reverse change can support a veto only when its resulting motif count reaches or passes the count before the remembered transition; both inverse signs must still qualify from the same transition. This allows partial restoration of repeated environments while retaining exclusions that undo their remembered abundance change. Earlier siblings required every live attribute, changed which transitions or motifs received credit, or retained overlapping origins. This experiment changes the quantitative meaning of one attribute match, with the existing attribute selection and lifecycle preserved. Four recorded opportunities remain vetoed even by the earlier complete-signature rule, so the new boundary addresses a different mismatch.

research_intent.falsifier: The implementation claim is falsified by a boundary taken from any event other than its selected accepted transition, an incorrect inverse inequality, a sign-only match treated as count-eligible while its endpoint remains short of the remembered count, a veto without both count-eligible inverse signs from one origin, or any new veto under identical Parent state and table.
